title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 31–35, June 1986). Grothendieck is axiomatizing a general notion of 'figure' for a tame 'analysis situs'. There is a set 𝓜 of elementary pieces (multistrata) and a set 𝓛 of 'lieux' (points). A set 𝓕_M of admissible figures carries two order relations: ≤ (being a sub-figure) and ≪ (being finer, or subordinate). There is also a compatibility relation ⋔. Page 33 listed the axioms Ax*1–5, for instance that every stratum carries a canonical multistrate structure Ã, and that A ⊂ B implies Ã ≪ B̃.

This page (dated 20 June) makes two points.

(1) Functoriality. The map 𝓛 → 𝓜 induces a pull-back map Fig(𝓜) → Fig(𝓛). This map is increasing for both ≤ and ≪. Composing it with the canonical map gives F ↦ multcont(F), the 'underlying set-theoretic multistructure' (the transcription's 'Multoub' should read 'multcont', as on p.35). That composite 𝓕 → Fig(𝓛) is also increasing for ≤ and ≪, and commutes with Sup and Inf for ≤. However, it is no longer necessarily injective: a structured figure is not determined by its underlying stratified point-set.

(2) Example 1A, the piecewise-linear (PL) model. Fix a topological space E. Let 𝓕 be the set of triples F = (X, Σ, Φ), where:
- X is a closed subset of E;
- Σ is a PL structure on X inducing its topology (perhaps of bounded dimension);
- Φ is a set-theoretic figure on X with support X, whose strata are closed PL subsets.

The orders are defined as follows.
- F' ≤ F iff X' ⊂ X is a PL subspace for Σ, Σ' is induced by Σ, and Φ' ≤ Φ.
- F' ≪ F iff the same first two conditions hold and Φ' ≪ Φ.

Here 𝓛 identifies with E, and the forgetful map F ↦ Φ is visibly not injective. For example, if E contains an arc [0,1], it carries many PL structures compatible with the topology (transport by non-PL homeomorphisms) that have the same underlying stratification.

Variant B starts a simplicial model. 𝓜 is the set of pairs (A, σ), with A ⊂ E and σ an affine-simplex structure on A, assumed continuous into E. Each such pair yields the face-stratification Φ_σ with |Φ_σ| = A. On p.35 the orders become 'sub-simplex', 'face-figure finer', and compatibility means 'intersection empty or a common face'. Figures there are finite (or locally finite) ≤-closed families of pairwise compatible simplices. The purpose of all this is to test the abstract axioms on concrete 'tame' geometric categories and to show that the passage to underlying point-set stratifications forgets structure.
errors: Notational slip in the definition of ≤: the right-hand side is written (X'',Σ'',Φ'') but the conditions refer to X, Σ, Φ.
'Fig(E) = Fig(E)' should presumably read Fig(𝓛) = Fig(E).
The claim that multcont commutes with Sup/Inf for ≤ is asserted without proof. It depends on existence of these Sup/Inf in 𝓕, which is not established on the page; plausible, but a gap.

For Variant B the continuity hypothesis is stated loosely ('l'inclusion A ⊂ E continue'). Presumably the requirement is that the topology of the simplex σ coincides with, or maps continuously to, the subspace topology of A.

ideas.what: Abstract framework of 'figures' (stratified subsets) with two orders, ≤ (sub-figure) and ≪ (refinement), plus a forgetful/pull-back map to set-theoretic multistructures that is monotone and Sup/Inf-preserving
ideas.modern_name: axiomatic tame topology / abstract stratified spaces (compare o-minimal structures, posets of stratifications)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tame topology programme announced by Grothendieck in Esquisse (1984); o-minimality by van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s)
ideas.where_published: Only the programmatic sketch in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 (topologie modérée); this axiomatics is unpublished

ideas.what: Non-injectivity of structured figure → underlying stratification, e.g. distinct PL structures on an arc with the same stratification
ideas.modern_name: forgetful functor PL → TOP stratified sets is not faithful on objects

ideas.what: PL model of figures: triples (closed subset, PL structure, PL-stratification), and simplicial variant with face-stratifications and compatibility = intersection is a common face
ideas.modern_name: PL stratified spaces / geometric simplicial complexes in a space

missed.claim: The page is part of an unpublished 1986 attempt to axiomatize 'figures' abstractly via two orders (≤, ≪) and compatibility, tested on PL and simplicial models. The aim is a foundation for tame topology independent of any chosen model (PL, semialgebraic, etc.). This axiomatic approach, distinct from o-minimality, was not developed further in the literature.
missed.quote: l'application 𝓕 → Fig(𝓛) F ↦ multcont(F) est également croissante pour ≤ et ≪, et commute aux Sup pour ≤, et à Inf pour ≤. Mais elle n'est plus nécessairement injective.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It offers an order-theoretic, model-independent formalism for stratified 'tame' geometry. This could be compared with o-minimal structures and with poset-indexed and exit-path approaches to stratified spaces (Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka). However, the content on this page is mostly elementary examples.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine illustrative page: monotonicity of a forgetful map, plus the observation that PL and simplicial structures are not determined by their underlying stratifications. The only interest is that it documents Grothendieck's unpublished 1986 axiomatic tame-topology programme, which is known in outline from the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: Margin note '[transformations sous-figures en sous-figures]' likely reads 'transforme sous-figures en sous-figures'.
'induisant[?] ... sur X' likely 'induisant la topologie (donnée) sur X'.
'On a ensuite les relations' is probably 'On définit ensuite les relations' or similar.
The non-injectivity example should read 'p. ex. si E contient une partie homéomorphe à [0,1]' (as on p.35).
In the definition of ≤, the right-hand member (X'',Σ'',Φ'') is likely meant to be (X,Σ,Φ) (Grothendieck's own slip).
